review.summary: Mercedes lead the championship with 578 points across 17 rounds, 11 wins and 22 podiums. Antonelli tops the drivers' standings on 340, ahead of Russell on 238, so there is a clear gap between them though both score regularly.
review.lastRace: At the Singapore Grand Prix Antonelli finished third from fourth on the grid, taking 15 points, while Russell recovered to ninth after starting 19th for two points.

review.lastRace: At the Singapore Grand Prix Leclerc finished second from second on the grid for 18 points, while Hamilton came home sixth after starting third to claim eight points.

review.summary: McLaren are third with 339 points after 17 rounds, two wins and seven podiums. Norris sits sixth on 201, ahead of team-mate Piastri on 138, giving them a comfortable margin between the two drivers.
review.lastRace: At the Singapore Grand Prix Norris finished fourth from fifth for 12 points and Piastri fifth from sixth for 10 points, both scoring cleanly.

At the Grand Prix of Indonesia they swept the front four: Bezzecchi won, Raul Fernandez second, Martin third and Ai Ogura fourth.

review.summary: DS Penske are ninth with 91 points after 17 rounds, one win and a single podium. Taylor Barnard leads in eleventh on 68 points, while Maximilian Günther sits eighteenth on 23 — a wide gap between the two.
review.lastRace: A breakthrough round for DS Penske as Barnard took his first victory, climbing from sixth to win and taking 25 points, though Günther faded to eleventh from fourteenth without points.

Raul Fernandez finished second for SuperFile Trackhouse and Jorge Martin third for Aprilia Racing.
Pedro Acosta was fifth for Red Bull KTM Factory Racing with Marc Marquez sixth.
Four riders did not finish: Toprak Razgatlioglu, Jack Miller, Francesco Bagnaia and Fermin Aldeguer.

review.summary: Taylor Barnard drove through the field from sixth to take his first victory for DS Penske, while Nyck De Vries converted his pole into second for Mahindra and teammate Edoardo Mortara took third from second. The classification showed a front-row fade as Pascal Wehrlein dropped from third to fourteenth and Nico Müller from fourth to twelfth.

Norman Nato climbed nine places from nineteenth on the grid to finish tenth and score a point for Nissan.
Nyck De Vries converted his pole position into second for Mahindra, with teammate Edoardo Mortara taking third from second on the grid.
Porsche's Pascal Wehrlein dropped from third to fourteenth as both front-row cars faded.
